- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap upward revisions after spikes.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 73+), leading to over-forecasted 30d peaks; apply downward bias to 3–5 day horizon after spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10–15 day average is >70, model often forecasts >72; if <68, model often forecasts <68; adjust toward historical mean of last 18 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses 1–2 day trend shifts; add 1–2 day lag correction for sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.7→0.8→0.9), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment step above 0.7.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., 0.8→0.1), model often fails to adjust downward; apply 1–2% downward correction to 30d forecast.
